capitals.name: Kuku (Koukou)
capitals.note: The page calls Koukou the capital, 'on a promontory with about 15,000 inhabitants' (no date), and names Aourir and Achallam as earlier seats (no dates); it gives no coordinates. The dot is placed at Tizi-Ouzou, the gazetteer's nearest town, and is only about right.

correction.text: Greater Kabylie with the lands 'from the Djurdjura to Sétif and Constantine' that the Belkadis ruled before 1518

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The infobox gives c. 1515 for the founding (Louis Rinn: 1510). The page has no area figure; the Sétif and Constantine provinces are drawn whole, which overstates a Belkadi sphere, and the Ait Abbas country between them is not subtracted.

correction.text: roughly Greater Kabylie, after 'the break with the Barbarossas in 1518'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'After the break with the Barbarossas in 1518, the domain shrank to roughly Greater Kabylie.' Tizi Ouzou and Boumerdès provinces are my reading of Greater Kabylie.

correction.text: Greater Kabylie and Algiers, seized by Belkadi in 1520

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'De facto king of Koukou and Algiers from 1520 to 1525/1527'; the Ahmed ou el Kadhi page has him capture Algiers in 1520 and rule it until 1527 'when Hayreddin reclaimed control'. The Hafsid dossier's Algiers loss is 1525.

correction.text: Greater Kabylie, the Kuku country, with no frontier change on the page

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no border change after 1525/1527 and says the Ath l-Qadi dynasty ruled 'until 1632 or 1638'. Bridging.

region.text: Greater Kabylie, Sétif and Constantine, 'from the Djurdjura to Sétif and Constantine'

ledger.note: c. 1515: the kingdom of Kuku is founded. The page 'was established around 1515 CE' (infobox c. 1515; Louis Rinn gives 1510; the Ahmed ou el Kadhi infobox has his reign from 1510). Before 1518 'the Belkadis ruled from the Djurdjura to Sétif and Constantine, allied with the Barbarossas'; the page does not tie that extent to 1515.
1518: the break with the Barbarossas. 'After the break with the Barbarossas in 1518, the domain shrank to roughly Greater Kabylie'; the page does not say who took Sétif and Constantine.

1520: Belkadi takes Algiers. 'He captured Algiers in 1520 and ruled it until 1527, when Hayreddin reclaimed control' (with 'support from the Hafsids of Tunis'); the Kuku page: 'de facto king of Koukou and Algiers from 1520 to 1525/1527', and the Koukou troops 'betrayed Barbarossa, who fled Algiers' in 1520.

1525: Hayreddin retakes Algiers. The Kuku page ends Belkadi's rule of Algiers in '1525/1527'; the Ahmed ou el Kadhi page has him die in 1527 at Thénia 'after a brutal battle against Hayreddin Barbarossa'. 1525 is the earlier reading, kept to agree with the Hafsid dossier's 1525 loss.

1632 or 1638: the Ath l-Qadi dynasty ends. The page says it ruled 'until 1632 or 1638 CE' and names no successor; 1638 is the later reading. Si Amar was assassinated in 1618 by his brother Mohamed, and Si Ahmed Atounsi 'regained the throne with Hafsid troops'.

wars.name: Belkadi and the Hafsids against the Barbarossas at Algiers
wars.outcome: Hafsid reinforcements helped Belkadi defeat Hayreddin at Issers in 1519; Belkadi took Algiers in 1520; Hayreddin reclaimed it in 1525/1527 and Ahmed ou el Kadhi died in 1527 at Thénia.
wars.note: The Ahmed ou el Kadhi page gives no year for the Issers battle; the Kuku page gives 1519. The Hafsid dossier has the same war as 1520-1525.

certainty.note: The pages give no frontier: Greater Kabylie as Tizi Ouzou and Boumerdès provinces, and Sétif and Constantine whole, are the researcher's.

notes: Cliopatria has no Kuku row. The Hafsid dossier already holds the 1520 and 1525 Algiers events under the counterpart regency-of-algiers; the Regency dossier itself starts in 1706, so the counterpart slug has no dossier for 1520-1525 (the Regency page dates the state from 1516). The Kuku page says the kingdom was 'an absolutely independent feudatory' that paid an unspecified tribute to the Algiers pashalik (no date), that Hassan Pasha married the king's daughter for an alliance (no year), and that Koukou troops served in the Algerian campaigns of 1541, 1562, 1565, 1569, 1576 and 1578 and the sieges of the Qala (1559); the tribute is the Regency's to record. Its mention that Cherchell and Annaba gave allegiance in 1520-1527 has no exact year and is not drawn. The Hafsid dossier has Constantine pass to Algiers in the 1530s, the Kuku page has it a Belkadi land before 1518; the two are not reconciled. Ahmed ou el Kadhi's reign is 1510-1527 on his page and 1515-1527 on the kingdom's infobox. The Ait Abbas kingdom (kingdom-of-beni-abbas) was its rival: its Ahmed Amokrane is said to have occupied Algiers in 1598. The 1618 Aourir move of Si Ahmed Atounsi and the 1696 succession of Si Ali (a date after the stated end of the dynasty, which the page does not explain) are not drawn.
